questions.question: Look at 3, 6, 9, 12. What number is added each time?
questions.explain: From 3 to 6, you count 4, 5, 6 — that is 3 more. Every step adds 3. The trap is to pick a number you already see in the list, like 6.

questions.question: Look at 5, 8, 11, 14. How many do you add each time?
questions.explain: From 5 to 8 is 3 more. Same from 8 to 11. The rule is always add 3. Do not pick a number from the list as the answer.

questions.question: Look at 10, 15, 20, 25. What is added each time?
questions.explain: From 10 to 15 is 5 more. Same from 15 to 20. The rule is add 5 each time. The trap is to pick 10 just because it is the first number in the list.

questions.question: Look at 7, 9, 11, 13. How many more each time?
questions.explain: From 7 to 9 is 2 more. From 9 to 11 is also 2 more. The rule is add 2 each time. Do not pick 7 or 9 just because they are in the list.

questions.question: Mia collects shells. She has 4, then 7, then 10, then 13. How many more shells each time?
questions.explain: From 4 to 7 is 3 more. From 7 to 10 is also 3 more. Mia adds 3 shells each time. The trap is to pick 4 or 7 from the list.

questions.question: Tom stacks blocks. Row 1 has 5, row 2 has 8, row 3 has 11. How many more blocks in each new row?
questions.explain: From 5 to 8 is 3 more. Each new row has 3 more blocks. Do not pick 5 or 8 — those are numbers in the list, not the rule.

questions.question: A snail climbs 6 cm, then 9 cm, then 12 cm, then 15 cm. How many cm does it add each time?
questions.explain: From 6 to 9 is 3 more. Each step the snail adds 3 cm. The number 6 is where it starts, not how much it adds.

questions.question: Lily saves 3 dollars, then 7, then 11, then 15. How many dollars more each time?
questions.explain: From 3 to 7 is 4 more. From 7 to 11 is also 4 more. Lily adds 4 dollars each time. The trap is to pick 3 or 7 from the list.

questions.question: A pattern is 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. Sam says the rule is add 4 each time. What is wrong with Sam's answer?
questions.explain: From 6 to 9 is 3 more, not 4. Sam counted the gap wrong. The real rule is add 3 each time.

questions.question: One pattern is 4, 7, 10, 13. Another is 2, 6, 10, 14. Which one adds a bigger number each time?
questions.explain: The first adds 3 each time. The second adds 4 each time. So the second adds a bigger number. The trap is to guess without checking both gaps.

questions.question: A pattern is 8, 12, 16, 20. Jay says the rule is add 8 each time. What should Jay say instead?
questions.explain: From 8 to 12 is 4 more. Jay picked 8 because it is the first number, but the rule is add 4 each time.

questions.question: A pattern is 6, 11, 16, 21. Priya says it adds 6 each time. What is the real rule?
questions.explain: From 6 to 11 is 5 more, not 6. Priya picked the starting number by mistake. The real rule is add 5 each time.
